title: Local emergency text files
summary: On degrade xtpd runs from plain text in /etc/xtpd/emergency/: services.txt (service, class, hook, protection), peers.txt (peer, layer, carrier, address; also fills xtp_peers), service.keys (XTP key-file format, mode 600), classes.txt (planner disposition syntax), state.txt (declared state and reason; an operator edit forces it). In NORMAL xtpd rewrites the set from LDAP after every good refresh (write, sync, rename) with time and LDAP epoch at the top. One strict parser: no symbolic links, owner and mode checked, bad lines reported by number while good lines stay in force. mu_audit checks existence, mode and freshness.
authority: design (architecture Tom Dyer; written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: One record per line, readable from a serial console
A degrade switches the source; nothing is reconfigured during an emergency
A stale emergency set is an audit finding
procedure: Keep the set current in NORMAL; never edit it except to force a state in an emergency

provenance.claim: Per-service keys, LDAP first then a mode-600 key file; protected FIRST checked before any state
